newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ futures end flat to weaker in dull trade.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ futures end flat to weaker in dull trade.

text.p: FCOJ futures erased early gains amid closed flat to slightly lower on Tuesday, but prices continued to be confined to tight ranges and interest remained thin, traders said.
"Dull is the word," said one trader. "There hasn't been much action, it's just moving sideways."

September juice settled unchanged, at 75.15 cents a lb, after ranging from 75.65 to 74.80 cents. November sagged 0.10 cent, to 77.10 cents, while the rest of the board closed down 0.25 to up 0.05 cent.

New York juice futures headed higher in the morning, bolstered by light speculative buying, dealers said. But trade selling thwarted further gains and kept the market under pressure in the afternoon, they said.
Dealers said they continued to expect the market to trade quietly ahead of a private estimate of the 1997/98 Florida crop by Citrus Consulting International, on August 14.
"People are just standing aside until the 14th," said a broker.

Until some fresh fundamentals emerge, traders said plentiful supplies -- with back-to-back record harvests expected in top-growers Florida and Brazil -- were likely to keep the market's bias to the downside.
On the charts, September support was pegged at 73.50 cents, followed by 71.30 cents, while resistance was seen at 78.00 cents and then 80.00 cents.
An estimated 1,800 lots changed hands on the day, compared with Monday's official tally of 1,561 lots.
